meta.source_provenance: Email from Ben Carter to PC Jon Dixon on 8 Mar 2025 at 19:00 (provided by user)

emails.subject_summary: Statement preference, mental health impact, medical report guidance request
emails.body:
Hello mate, I'd rather give a statement face to face, it was your call that woke me up today, I'm not sleeping well. If you could let me know in advance, mentally a phone call out the blue at the moment you could get me in any of my up and down manic or depressed states; if I know in advance the time and date, I can prepare myself for going through it. Every time I have to go through the evidence I go on a downward spiral; it brings up so much pain. I've contacted the doctor to call me back and I'm going to arrange an appointment too.

The doctor has said for a fee they will provide whatever you need, could you please highlight what to really concentrate on, what I should say to them when creating/writing up this medical report so as not to miss anything. A lot of it is emails which they don't keep hold of for longer than 90 days; I could send them all the emails and they could confirm these have been received, etc...

Happy to pay whatever; I'm already in so much debt due to her, I might as well go in more debt if it's going to help my case and the justice I deserve. I took your advice—I got out. I felt like I let down the speed of the investigation by not providing a statement and am seeing a friend tonight to start the process of confidence again as I need to be strong now.

Thanks so much for taking this seriously. I still have all the words she's said about me in my head and doubt the system as she told me they won't listen, and stalking cases are harder when the gender are this way round. Thank you.

Ben Carter
